Harness engineering guide, the first weekly digest, and a This week link

- comparisons/harness-engineering.md: what harness engineering is, where
  the term came from (Hashimoto, Feb 5 2026; OpenAI, Feb 11), and eight
  practices, each mapped to the projects in this list that do it, with
  their autonomy, recovery, and complexity ratings. The term is the
  field's name for this work, and the README used it three times.
- latest-changes.md and changes.json: the first digest, covering Sep 13 to
  Oct 18 (21 new harnesses, top star gains, the new guide, skills, and
  templates). It replaces best-of-nix content left from June.
- README: a This week link under the site link, and whats_new in the MCP
  tool list.

pull requests waited; every routine curation PR (#102 to #141) closed
unmerged. Each candidate was re-checked against the GitHub API (stars,
license, commits, archived, last push); decisions and reasons are in the
maintainer's curation log.

Weekly digest: a release, a /changes/ page, and whats_new every Sunday

The list stopped showing up in GitHub feeds after Sep 14: the last release
was list-2026-09-2, and latest-changes.md still held best-of-nix content
from June (left over from best-of-update-action). best-of lists publish a
release on every update, which lands in each stargazer's home feed.

- scripts/weekly_digest.py diffs last week's harnesses.json against the new
  one: harnesses added or removed, biggest star gains, fastest growers,
  newly archived repos, new guides, skills, and templates. It writes
  latest-changes.md and appends to changes.json (52 weeks).
- weekly-rescore.yml runs it after generate.py and publishes the digest as
  a release (digest-YYYY-MM-DD); quiet weeks publish nothing.
- The site gets a /changes/ page (in the nav and sitemap) and serves
  changes.json.
- MCP server 0.8.0: whats_new(since?, limit?) reads changes.json, so
  agents can answer "what's new in agent harnesses".
- Every project page now offers the CONTRIBUTING.md badge with a copy
  button. Only 1 of 166 listed projects used it, because no maintainer was
  ever shown it.
- list_categories docstring and the MCP README no longer hard-code "10
  categories" (there are 12).
